transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I, uh… I’m here because I lost my temper on a board call. It was over a small question about the facility budget, and I snapped at someone. That’s… not how I run my company, or how I treat people.
Has losing your temper like that happened to you before?
Not like that, no. I mean… I’ve been firm before, sure, but snapping on a board call over a facility budget question—that’s not me. That’s not how I run things.
Has anything significant happened in your life recently that's been causing you a lot of stress?
Yes. About six days ago there was… an explosion and a fire during a walkthrough. Since then, things have been… off.
Have you been acting impulsively in other situations since the explosion and fire?
I don’t know. Not really that I’ve noticed. That call was the one that made me think… something’s not right.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts or ideas that you can't seem to get out of your head since the explosion and fire?

Yes. It… comes back on its own. I’ll be in the middle of a call, or just looking over numbers, and suddenly I’m seeing the blast and the fire by the loading area again. Like a bad film I didn’t ask to watch.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of the explosion and fire?
Yeah… I have. I’ve been staying away from the new building. And there’s a mortgage folder, safety reports… I just leave them sitting there. Soon as I go to open them, my stomach drops, so I don’t.
Have you been easily startled since the explosion and fire?
Yes… more than I’d like. If a door slams or the printer starts up behind me, I jump hard, like it’s happening again. Takes me a few minutes to settle my hands.
Have you been having difficulty falling or staying asleep since the explosion and fire?
I… don’t know. Sleep’s been a little off, maybe, but I can’t say it’s because of that. I haven’t really been keeping track.
Have you been having trouble concentrating since the explosion and fire?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I’ve had a few distracted moments, but I can’t say it’s anything different than usual. I haven’t paid close attention to it.
How long have you been seeing the blast and the fire by the loading area in your mind?
About… six days now. Since that walkthrough, when the explosion and fire happened.
How disturbing are these memories of the blast and the fire when they come back to you?
It’s… unpleasant. It kind of jumps back into my head in the middle of a call, or when I’m looking at numbers. Like a bad film I didn’t ask to see. I don’t like it, but… I try to push it aside.
Do you feel like these memories of the blast and the fire are causing you a lot of distress?

I wouldn’t say a lot, exactly. It’s just… in the middle of a call, or when I’m looking at numbers, it jumps back in my head—the blast, the fire by the loading area. Like a bad film I didn’t ask to see. It bothers me, yes.
Do you feel guilty about what happened during the explosion and fire?
I don’t know. Guilty… not really how I’d put it. It was just… a bad situation.
Are there any specific things you're avoiding because they remind you of the explosion and fire?

A few things, I guess. I’ve been staying away from the new building. And there’s a mortgage folder, safety reports… they’re just sitting there unopened. When I go to pick them up, my stomach just drops, so I leave them.
Have you been feeling detached from people or things that normally matter to you since the explosion and fire?
A little, maybe. I still sit with my wife at dinner, and I look at my chess problems or hiking notes, but… it’s flat. Like I know those things should settle me, and I just can’t quite get there.
How long have you been avoiding the new building and those documents like the mortgage folder and safety reports?
About six days now. Since the walkthrough… when the explosion and fire happened.
Do you feel like you're able to experience a full range of emotions like you used to before the explosion and fire?
Not really. I mean… I can get through dinner with my wife, look at a chess problem or my hiking notes, but it all feels kind of flat. Like I know I should enjoy it, but I just don’t quite get there.
Have you lost interest in things you normally enjoy doing since the explosion and fire?
Yeah… somewhat. The usual things—chess, my hiking notes, even dinner with my wife—they just feel flat. I know they should help, but I can’t really get there.
How long have you been feeling detached from people or things that normally matter to you?
About six days. Since that walkthrough… the explosion and fire. It’s been like that since then.
